microwave_time.user_tendencies: Prefers 2 min for most meals to achieve warm serving temperature. IF meal is fruit or dessert with intended cold serving temperature THEN no microwave BECAUSE proper food temperature enhances enjoyment. IF user is in a hurry THEN 1 min BECAUSE reduces overall meal time even if food is slightly cooler. IF user is relaxed with ample time THEN 3 min BECAUSE allows food to reach optimal warmth for comfort.

robot_speed.user_tendencies: Prefers medium speed as baseline for smooth, comfortable operation. IF user is in a hurry THEN fast BECAUSE reduces overall meal duration. IF user is in a social setting with another person nearby THEN slow BECAUSE slower movements feel less intrusive to social partners and create more comfortable interaction dynamics. IF user is fatigued THEN slow BECAUSE reduced cognitive load from slower, more predictable movements. IF user is in a social setting AND fatigued THEN slow BECAUSE fatigue amplifies social discomfort, taking precedence.

skewering_axis.user_tendencies: Prefers perpendicular skewering as default because user has good mouth opening and perpendicular orientation increases bite acquisition success. IF food items are very fibrous or stringy (e.g., certain vegetables) THEN parallel to major axis BECAUSE parallel skewering handles these foods more reliably. IF user is in a hurry THEN perpendicular to major axis BECAUSE maximizes acquisition success and reduces retry delays. IF user has just eaten multiple bites and jaw is tiring THEN parallel to major axis BECAUSE narrower bites reduce jaw strain even though acquisition may be slightly less reliable.

confirm_feeding_pickup.user_tendencies: Prefers auto-continue confirmation as baseline to balance safety with efficiency. IF user is eating alone in a quiet personal setting THEN no BECAUSE failed pickups are not socially awkward and reduces interaction overhead. IF user is in a social setting with another person nearby THEN yes (without any auto-continue) BECAUSE explicit control prevents embarrassing empty-fork transfers that would distract conversation partners. IF user is fatigued AND in a personal setting THEN no BECAUSE minimizes button presses and mental load. IF user is fatigued AND in a social setting THEN yes (with auto-continue countdown) BECAUSE fatigue makes explicit confirmation burdensome, but social context requires some safety check; auto-continue compromise allows intervention if needed but doesn't force action.

confirm_navigation_arrival.user_tendencies: Prefers auto-continue confirmation as baseline while parking positions are being learned and refined. IF user has been using the robot for multiple meals AND parking has proven reliable THEN no BECAUSE eliminates unnecessary confirmation pages once learned positions are accurate. IF user is in a social setting THEN yes (with auto-continue countdown) BECAUSE maintains some oversight without requiring active intervention, reducing awkward pauses during social meals. IF user is in a hurry THEN yes (with auto-continue countdown) BECAUSE preserves learning refinement but auto-continue prevents slowdown. IF user is fatigued AND in a personal setting THEN no BECAUSE minimizes interaction burden once basic parking is established.

confirm_manipulation.user_tendencies: Prefers auto-continue confirmation as baseline for safety during object manipulations. IF user is eating alone in a quiet personal setting AND the robot has performed >10 successful manipulations in prior meals THEN no BECAUSE reliable detections can be trusted automatically. IF user is in a social setting with another person nearby THEN yes (with auto-continue countdown) BECAUSE provides safety oversight without creating lengthy pauses that interrupt social dynamics. IF user is in a hurry THEN yes (with auto-continue countdown) BECAUSE auto-continue preserves speed while maintaining detection refinement. IF user is fatigued THEN yes (with auto-continue countdown) BECAUSE fatigue reduces ability to actively monitor, but auto-continue ensures progress without forcing manual intervention.

transfer_mode.user_tendencies: Prefers outside-mouth transfer as baseline because user can lean forward comfortably and this preserves autonomy. IF user is fatigued or has low energy THEN inside mouth transfer BECAUSE eliminates need to lean forward, reducing physical exertion when energy is limited. IF user is in a social setting and fatigued THEN inside mouth transfer BECAUSE fatigue overrides social preference; maintaining comfort takes precedence over social norms. IF user is relaxed with ample time THEN outside mouth transfer BECAUSE allows leisurely interaction and active participation. IF user is energetic THEN outside mouth transfer BECAUSE user enjoys active engagement in the feeding process.

outside_mouth_distance.user_tendencies: Applies only when transfer_mode is outside mouth transfer; otherwise is not applicable. Prefers medium distance as baseline for comfortable reach without requiring excessive leaning. IF user is fatigued THEN near BECAUSE reduces required reach distance and physical effort. IF user is energetic and in a personal setting THEN far BECAUSE user enjoys engaging more actively in the transfer. IF user is in a social setting THEN medium BECAUSE balances social comfort (not too close to face) with reasonable effort. IF user is in a hurry THEN near BECAUSE minimizes time spent extending reach and reduces overall transfer duration.

convey_robot_ready_for_initiating_transf.user_tendencies: Prefers multimodal cue (speech + LED) as baseline for clear, redundant signaling. IF user is watching television or working on a device THEN speech + LED BECAUSE visual and auditory redundancy ensures user notices cue despite environmental distractions. IF user is in a quiet personal setting THEN LED BECAUSE sufficient without adding speech overhead. IF user is in a social setting with another person nearby THEN speech + LED BECAUSE helps both the user and social partner understand robot state, supporting conversational flow. IF user is fatigued THEN speech + LED BECAUSE multimodal cues reduce cognitive load of interpreting single-modality signals.

detect_user_ready_for_initiating_transfe.user_tendencies: Prefers button as baseline because user has good arm control and button provides explicit, reliable signaling. IF user is in a social setting with another person nearby THEN button BECAUSE open-mouth detection risks being confused with talking, creating awkward false triggers. IF user is fatigued AND in a personal setting THEN open mouth BECAUSE button pressing is effortful when fatigued; open-mouth detection requires no active effort. IF user is fatigued AND in a social setting THEN button BECAUSE even though open-mouth would reduce effort, social context prevents its use due to talking confusion; explicit button press is necessary compromise. IF user is in a hurry THEN autocontinue BECAUSE eliminates decision latency, though user may prefer button in social settings even when rushed due to talking-confusion risk.

Prefers button as baseline because user has good arm control and provides explicit signaling. IF user is in a social setting THEN button BECAUSE open-mouth detection risks confusion with talking; button avoids false triggers during conversation. IF user is fatigued AND in a personal setting THEN open mouth BECAUSE minimizes physical effort when energy is limited. IF user is fatigued AND in a social setting THEN button BECAUSE fatigue would make open-mouth easier, but social talking-confusion risk takes precedence; button provides necessary social compatibility. IF user is in a hurry THEN autocontinue BECAUSE eliminates decision latency, though button remains preferred in social contexts regardless of time pressure.

Prefers button as baseline for explicit control over mouth-wiping initiation. IF user is in a social setting THEN button BECAUSE open-mouth detection could be confused with talking; button provides unambiguous signal. IF user is fatigued AND in a personal setting THEN open mouth BECAUSE reduces physical effort of button pressing. IF user is fatigued AND in a social setting THEN button BECAUSE social context constraint overrides fatigue preference; talking-confusion risk necessitates button despite fatigue. IF user is in a hurry THEN autocontinue BECAUSE reduces decision overhead, though button remains preferred in social settings due to talking-confusion risk.

convey_robot_ready_for_completing_transf.user_tendencies: Prefers multimodal cue (speech + LED) as baseline for clear signal that transfer location is reached. IF user is watching television or working on a device THEN speech + LED BECAUSE ensures user notices cue despite environmental distraction. IF user is in a quiet personal setting THEN LED BECAUSE sufficient without adding speech. IF user is in a social setting with another person nearby THEN speech + LED BECAUSE helps both user and social partner understand robot state. IF user is fatigued THEN speech + LED BECAUSE multimodal redundancy reduces cognitive load in detecting readiness signal.

detect_user_completed_transfer_feeding.user_tendencies: Prefers perception (force-torque sensing) as baseline because it is reliable and requires no user action. IF user is in a social setting where perception-based detection might feel unnatural THEN button BECAUSE explicit completion signal feels more socially appropriate than robot-detected bite completion. IF user is fatigued THEN perception BECAUSE eliminates need for button press at the end of each bite; passive detection reduces effort. IF user is fatigued AND in a social setting THEN perception BECAUSE fatigue amplifies social fatigue benefit of passive sensing over button-pressing burden; perception takes precedence. IF user is in a hurry THEN perception BECAUSE fastest completion detection, eliminating user decision latency.

detect_user_completed_transfer_drinking.user_tendencies: Prefers button as baseline because head-nod detection (perception alternative) can feel unnatural and is less reliable for drinking completion. IF user is fatigued AND in a personal setting THEN perception BECAUSE head-nod detection, though potentially awkward, eliminates button pressing effort. IF user is fatigued AND in a social setting THEN button BECAUSE even though perception would reduce effort, unnatural head-nod gesture in social context is socially awkward; button provides natural alternative. IF user is in a hurry THEN perception BECAUSE head-nod detection is faster than button press. IF user is in a social setting THEN button BECAUSE head-nod gesture feels unnatural during social meal; explicit button press is more socially appropriate.

detect_user_completed_transfer_wiping.user_tendencies: Prefers button as baseline because head-nod detection (perception alternative) can feel awkward for mouth-wiping completion. IF user is fatigued AND in a personal setting THEN perception BECAUSE head-nod detection eliminates button pressing when energy is limited. IF user is fatigued AND in a social setting THEN button BECAUSE social context makes head-nod gesture feel unnatural; button provides socially appropriate alternative despite fatigue. IF user is in a hurry THEN perception BECAUSE head-nod detection is faster than button press. IF user is in a social setting THEN button BECAUSE head-nod gesture during social meal feels awkward; explicit button signal is more appropriate.

retract_between_bites.user_tendencies: Prefers retracting between bites as baseline for maintaining unobstructed view and supporting interaction. IF user is eating alone in a quiet personal setting THEN no BECAUSE reduces meal duration without social discomfort or distraction concerns. IF user is in a social setting with another person nearby THEN yes BECAUSE prevents robot from obstructing social partner's view, maintaining conversation comfort. IF user is watching television or working on a device THEN yes BECAUSE prevents robot from blocking screen view during engagement. IF user is in a hurry THEN no BECAUSE retracting delays meal completion; speed takes precedence over view preservation in personal settings. IF user is fatigued AND eating alone THEN no BECAUSE fatigue makes even short retracting movements less preferred; minimizing movement helps conserve energy in personal contexts where obstruction is not a concern.

bite_dipping_preference.user_tendencies: Prefers more dipping as baseline to maximize flavor enjoyment in personal settings. IF food does not have available sauces or dips THEN do not dip BECAUSE no dipping opportunity exists. IF user is in a social setting with another person nearby THEN less BECAUSE excessive dipping risks messiness that could be socially awkward; lighter dipping maintains cleanliness. IF user is eating alone and relaxed THEN more BECAUSE allows fuller flavor experience without social concerns. IF user is in a hurry THEN less BECAUSE reduces dipping time, though primary constraint is dipping availability. IF user is fatigued THEN less BECAUSE reduces manipulation complexity; lighter dipping is simpler for the robot and user.

bite_ordering.user_tendencies: Default to no particular order when no evidence of preference exists. IF meal contains both proteins and vegetables THEN alternate between protein bites and vegetable bites to balance flavors throughout the meal. IF meal contains items with significantly different temperatures THEN serve hotter items first while they remain at optimal warmth. IF meal contains a primary item and a sauce THEN pair dippable items with their corresponding sauces as they are served. IF user is in a social setting AND meal contains messy items THEN save messiest items for later in the meal to maintain appearance during conversation.

wait_before_autocontinue_seconds.user_tendencies: Prefers 30 seconds as baseline balance between providing sufficient intervention time and maintaining reasonable meal pace. IF user is in a hurry THEN 15 sec BECAUSE reduces total meal time; shorter wait encourages efficiency. IF user is fatigued THEN 60 sec BECAUSE extended wait reduces pressure to respond quickly when reaction time is slower; allows comfortable pacing. IF user is relaxed with ample time THEN 60 sec BECAUSE allows unhurried decision-making without time pressure. IF user is fatigued AND in a social setting THEN 30 sec BECAUSE while fatigue suggests longer wait, social context prevents excessive pauses that disrupt interaction flow; 30 seconds provides compromise. IF user is in a noisy environment (e.g., watching TV) THEN 60 sec BECAUSE longer wait accommodates attention shifts caused by environmental distraction.
